source.title: Retrieval-induced forgetting: evidence for a recall-specific mechanism

confidence_rationale: Classic dissociation showing that active inhibition (engaged specifically by competitive RECALL) produces forgetting that mere strengthening/re-exposure does not -- evidence that inhibition and strength-based competition are distinct mechanisms with distinct consequences. Directly supports Q-058's second sub-question (inhibition vs competition are not the same thing) and its third (the mechanism is engaged context-specifically, in the act of recall). Confidence moderate: human behavioural psychology, single classic study, indirect mapping to REE inter-field couplings.
failure_signatures: Strengthening practiced items (re-exposure) did NOT impair competitors, but competitive recall did -- so an REE model that treats competition purely as relative-strength normalisation (softmax) will MISS the inhibitory suppression that only appears when the loser is actively retrieved against.
The inhibitory effect is recall-specific: it is engaged by the act of retrieval, implying competition modes are not interchangeable across waking-action vs passive/offline regimes.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In the retrieval-practice paradigm, competitive recall of some category members (cue: 'fruit or__') impaired later recall of unpracticed members, whereas non-competitive re-exposure that strengthened the same items by an equal amount did NOT -- demonstrating that retrieval-induced forgetting is caused by inhibitory processes specific to the recall situation, not by increased strength-based competition.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports Q-058's claim that inhibition and competition are mechanistically distinct with different safety/behavioural consequences: a softmax/relative-strength competition (re-exposure analogue) does not produce the active suppression that a true inhibitory de-commit does. Bears on the MECH-090/MECH-105 decommitment distinction and on whether an explicit signed (inhibitory) edge is needed beyond local softmax (MECH-090/ARC-030/MECH-254).
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is human verbal-memory behaviour; the inhibition is inferred from recall accuracy, not measured at the circuit level. Mapping 'recall-specific inhibition' to REE inter-field decommitment couplings is a functional analogy, and the paradigm does not address simulation vs offline integration directly.
mapping.source_context: Human adults, taxonomic-category retrieval-practice paradigm; competitive vs non-competitive practice conditions matched for facilitation.

confidence_components.notes: Foundational, well-replicated paradigm (source quality good for behavioural psych), but a single classic study and an inferential, non-circuit measure; mapping to REE couplings is a functional analogy hence moderate fidelity and non-trivial transfer risk.
